steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: With only 3 replicates per design cell a deviating sample cannot simply be dropped — dropping one leaves n=2 in a cell and invalidates the interaction test. Flag the sample loudly and proceed; the DE step's Cook's-distance handling will mark affected genes NA.
The blind vst is for QC visualization only; do not feed the transformed values into the DE model.
steps.context: counts.csv is a 12,000 x 13 CSV (gene rows; 12 sample columns plus a gene id column) — gene-level counts from Salmon as delivered, length-correction state unknown. metadata.csv (12 rows x 4 columns) holds the sample name, condition, time (t0/t1), and time_hours. Read the actual condition and time level names from metadata.csv; model time as the categorical t0/t1, not time_hours. Single batch, no other covariates. The vst used here is blind to the design and is for QC only — the DE model is fit on raw counts in T1S2.
steps.question: Do the 12 samples (3 per condition x time cell, two condition levels x t0/t1) form a clean 2x2 structure with no outlier sample and no extreme library-size deviation, before the interaction model is fit?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf

steps.description: Sample-structure QC: per-sample library sizes, variance-stabilizing transformation (blind), PCA on the top-500 variable genes colored by condition and by time, and a heatmap of Euclidean distances between samples. Verify that the 12 sample columns of counts.csv align 1:1 with the 12 rows of metadata.csv. Assess whether the 2x2 structure is clean and whether any sample departs from its design cell.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot and sample distance heatmap produced and saved, both colored by condition and by time
The 12 sample columns of counts.csv verified to match the 12 rows of metadata.csv exactly (names and factor levels)
A written structure assessment: samples group by condition and time as expected, or any deviating sample is named explicitly
Library-size range across the 12 samples reported; any sample far below the median is flagged

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

With an interaction question and three or fewer replicates in a cell of the design, the interaction term has low power. The interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences, thus its standard error is larger than the standard error of a main effect at the same replicate number. Keep the interaction test as the primary result, but report the simple effects in each level beside it, with the same threshold. State the power limit in the report, and do not loosen the threshold to compensate. A gene that is absent from the interaction list is not shown to have the same effect in both levels.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.
steps.context: Gene x 12-sample count matrix after T1S1 QC; design factors condition (levels as named in metadata.csv) and time (t0/t1), 3 replicates per cell, unpaired, single batch. Reference levels and all contrasts must be set explicitly and reported. Note on shrinkage: this step carries the procedure's method of record (DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm-family log fold change shrinkage); the procedure's sourced setting selects ashr as the actual shrinkage estimator because every reported contrast in this 2x2 design is a multi-coefficient contrast (the interaction, and the simple effect in the non-reference time), and apeglm accepts a single coefficient only. Follow the setting: lfcShrink with ashr. The unshrunken estimate, lfcSE, and shrunken estimate are all reported; p-values come from the unshrunken fit.
steps.question: Does the treatment effect (difference between the two condition levels) differ between t0 and t1? Primary: the condition:time interaction Wald test. Secondary: the simple effects of condition at t0 and at t1, and the time main effect as descriptive.

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage per R-0029@22ca; the sourced setting selects ashr for the multi-coefficient interaction and simple-effect contrasts

steps.description: Minimal pre-filter (keep genes with >=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size; independent filtering in results does the rest), then fit the DESeq2 model design ~ condition + time + condition:time on the counts as delivered (no pre-normalization; median-of-ratios size factors inside the negative-binomial model). Test, in order: (1) the interaction contrast condition:time (primary, Wald test); (2) the simple effect of condition at the reference time (the main-effect coefficient); (3) the simple effect of condition at the other time (contrast = main effect + interaction); (4) the time main effect, descriptive only. Shrink LFCs with lfcShrink (ashr, per the sourced setting). Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast at alpha 0.05, passing the same alpha to results with independent filtering on. Cook's-distance outliers in cells with fewer than 7 replicates set p-values to NA: count them, report them separately from filter NAs, and list the flagged gene names. Inspect the unadjusted p-value histogram of each contrast before adjustment and describe its shape. State the expected power of the interaction test at 3 replicates per cell from the closed form (depth, dispersion, fold change, significance level; RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed), including the fold change the design can detect at 80% power for the interaction. Import state: no per-sample quantification files (quant.sf, abundance.h5, genes.results) and no average-transcript-length table accompany the Salmon gene table, so fit the counts as delivered with no length offset, check whether the matrix is integer-valued and report what was found, and state that the length offset is lost and a change in isoform use can appear as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table.
acceptance_criteria: A full results table for the interaction contrast with log2FoldChange, lfcSE, unshrunken and ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, Wald statistic, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value; significant genes defined by adjusted p < 0.05 only

Simple-effect tables for condition at t0 and at t1, each with its own within-contrast BH adjustment, plus the descriptive time main-effect table, every table labeled with its contrast name and the reference levels used
Unadjusted p-value histogram for each contrast saved, with a written reading of its shape (flat or decreasing from left OK; a hump or rise toward one is reported as a concern)
The count of genes with NA p-values from the Cook's-distance outlier flag reported separately from genes removed by the independent filter, with the flagged gene names listed

Power statement: expected power of the interaction test at 3 replicates per cell and the fold change detectable at 80% power, with the caution that more replicates raise power more than deeper sequencing

Import-state statement: counts used as delivered with no length offset (per the unknown length-correction state of the Salmon gene table), the integer/fractional check result, and the caveat that a change in isoform use can appear as differential expression

steps.name: Report
caveats: Do not present the interaction list alone as the answer: with 3 replicates per cell a gene absent from the significant interaction set is not shown to have the same treatment effect at both times; the simple effects must be read beside it.

The report constraint 'robustness = overlap_of_two_methods' assumes a second count model (edgeR quasi-likelihood). The procedure for this situation permits only the DESeq2 Wald test for the interaction question, so the overlap is reported as not run, with the reason stated — do not fabricate a second-method result.
A non-significant interaction is not evidence of no time dependence; state the power limit rather than interpreting absence as invariance.
steps.context: Consumes the T1S2 results (interaction contrast table, simple-effect tables for condition at t0 and t1, descriptive time main-effect table, unshrunken and ashr-shrunken LFCs, lfcSE, per-contrast p-value histograms, Cook's-distance NA counts and gene names, power statement, import-state statement) and the T1S1 QC plots. No new model is fitted in this step.
steps.question: Does the treatment effect differ between t0 and t1, and how defensible is that conclusion given 3 replicates per cell, the low power of the interaction term, and the unverified length correction of the Salmon gene table?

grounding.reason: no rule covers this step; the report constraints and settings are copied from the procedure skeleton as returned

For each gene, the simple effect of condition at the reference time, the simple effect at the other time, and the interaction contrast side by side, with the reference level of each factor named beside the table. The power statement (expected power at 3 replicates per cell, fold change detectable at 80%) before the gene tables. plan.title: Treatment × time interaction DE, 2×2 design
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are 12,000 genes x 12 samples: two condition levels x two time points (t0, t1), 3 biological replicates per design cell, single batch, human cell line, gene-level counts from Salmon as delivered. The research question — does the treatment effect differ between the two time points — is a 2x2 factorial interaction, so the analysis fits a fixed-effects negative-binomial model (condition + time + condition:time) and tests the interaction coefficient with the Wald test as the primary result, reporting the simple effects of condition at each time beside it. Sample-structure QC runs before the model because with 3 replicates per cell a single outlier sample would corrupt the interaction contrast. No per-sample quantification files or average-transcript-length table accompany the Salmon gene table, so the length-correction state is not established: the model is fit on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and that limitation is carried into the report (a change in isoform use can appear as differential expression). With 3 replicates per cell the interaction term has low power (it is a difference of two differences), so the design step states expected power from the closed form (RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed in the sandbox), and the report does not loosen the threshold to compensate. The two-method robustness overlap (DESeq2 vs edgeR QL) is not run in this situation because the procedure permits only the DESeq2 Wald test for the interaction question; the report states this explicitly and relies on the within-method diagnostics instead.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind-vst PCA on top variable genes plus sample distance heatmap (tpl-qc-eda@1.0.0)
DESeq2 minimal pre-filter then independent filtering in results
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors inside the count model
DESeq2 factorial design condition + time + condition:time on gene counts without length offset
DESeq2 Wald test on the interaction contrast, plus edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design for the overlap robustness check
lfcShrink with ashr for the interaction and simple-effect contrasts
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast with independent filtering on, p-value histogram inspected before adjustment
DESeq2 interaction report: simple effects and interaction contrast side by side, MA and dispersion diagnostics, power statement, DESeq2-edgeR overlap

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

With an interaction question and three or fewer replicates in a cell of the design, the interaction term has low power. The interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences, thus its standard error is larger than the standard error of a main effect at the same replicate number. Keep the interaction test as the primary result, but report the simple effects in each level beside it, with the same threshold. State the power limit in the report, and do not loosen the threshold to compensate. A gene that is absent from the interaction list is not shown to have the same effect in both levels.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind-vst PCA on top variable genes plus sample distance heatmap (tpl-qc-eda@1.0.0)
DESeq2 minimal pre-filter then independent filtering in results
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors inside the count model
DESeq2 factorial design condition + time + condition:time on gene counts without length offset
DESeq2 Wald test on the interaction contrast, plus edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design for the overlap robustness check
lfcShrink with ashr for the interaction and simple-effect contrasts
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast with independent filtering on, p-value histogram inspected before adjustment
DESeq2 interaction report: simple effects and interaction contrast side by side, MA and dispersion diagnostics, power statement, DESeq2-edgeR overlap
